🚨🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN: ARMY TAKES DOWN CARTEL BOSS THE U.S. HAD A $5M BOUNTY ON</u>

Mexico's Army detained Alfonso "Poncho La Quiringua" Fernández Magallón, boss of the Cártel de Los Reyes, in Imbarácuaro, Michoacán — a man U.S. authorities offered up to $5 million for, accused of drone attacks on Mexican soldiers in Cotija, Tingüindín and Jacona.

The cartel's answer was five roadblocks and burning vehicles in Los Reyes and Peribán. Security forces had them cleared within five hours. He now sits in FGR facilities in Mexico City.

Mexican intelligence, Mexican operation, Mexican results.

‍VOZ.US: Mexican Army arrests leader of Cartel de los Reyes, for whom the US had offered a $5 million reward August 2, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The Mexican Army captured Alfonso Fernández Magallón, alleged Cartel de los Reyes leader with a $5M US bounty, in Michoacán. The cartel answered with roadblocks and burning vehicles; security held. The US ambassador's response: a round of applause and a shared-commitment quote. 🇲🇽 Straight AFP-based write-up from a conservative US outlet — credit goes to Mexico's army and security cabinet, not Washington. • "set up roadblocks and set vehicles on fire" • "criminals have nowhere to hide"
banner: Army nabs cartel boss with $5M bounty

text: ‍KSL: Long-time Salt Lake resident deported to Mexico despite outcry by family and friends August 2, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Julio Irungaray Sr. lived in Utah for 35 years. ICE detained him June 24 and deported him within five days. DHS's response: "criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in our country." The criminal record: DUI convictions from 20-plus years ago, expunged, 17 years sober. 💀 KSL plays it straight — the DHS quote does all the work. • "did move pretty fast and ended up deporting him to Guadalajara, Mexico" • "criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in our country"
banner: 35 years in Utah, deported in days

text: ‍AP/US NEWS: Trump Administration Pushes Tougher English Rules for Mexican Train Crews Crossing Into the US July 31, 2026 | 🟡 📰 New FRA rule caps Mexican train crews at 10 miles inside the US over English proficiency. What AP notes almost in passing: the cross-border crew practice was built in 2018 — approved by the first Trump administration — to keep smugglers off idled trains. 🔍 Canadian crews do the exact same handoff over the northern border, routinely, no language rule attached. • "railroad crews must be able to communicate fully and accurately when crossing into the United States" • "the language barrier posed a hazard in the event of a derailment or other incident"
banner: English rule targets Mexican train crews

text: ‍TEXAS TRIBUNE: DACA mother of three suing the federal government over deportation to Mexico July 31, 2026 | 🟢 📰 DHS deported DACA recipient Jessica Treviño to Mexico in March. Then USCIS moved to terminate her status for "unauthorized travel outside of the United States" — the travel being her own deportation. Her three US-citizen children start school next month without her. 💀 The administration has deported 86 DACA recipients and arrested 241 more, per DHS's own letter to Sen. Durbin. • "unauthorized travel outside of the United States on or about March 25, 2026" • "This is what a deliberate, systematic effort to destroy DACA looks like in practice"
banner: DACA mom deported, blamed for own removal

text: ‍AP/ABC NEWS: Man whose slain brother led Mexican cartel pleads guilty to drug charges in US July 31, 2026 | 🟢 📰 AP ran the Antonio Oseguera Cervantes guilty plea straight — no editorializing. One thing the wire compresses: Mexico arrested him in December 2022 and extradited him north in February 2025. US courtroom wins start with Mexican captures. 🇲🇽 He was "transferred from Mexico to the U.S. for prosecution" — four words carrying a Mexican arrest, an extradition, and 92 cartel figures sent north under Sheinbaum. • "conspiring to traffic cocaine and methamphetamine into the U.S." • "faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years in prison"
banner: El Mencho's brother pleads guilty in US

🇲🇽🏭 <u>J.P. MORGAN: T-MEC RENEWAL WILL BE SIGNED — BUT NOT UNTIL NEXT YEAR</u>

“Everything is being configured” as a T-MEC renegotiation that stretches into 2027, says Gabriel Lozano, J.P. Morgan’s chief economist for Mexico — but the bank expects the renewal to be signed.

His warning: Mexico is riding the tech boom in non-auto manufacturing, yet without closing gaps in energy, water, connectivity and human capital it risks remaining the assembler while the US keeps the data centers and semiconductors. “Mexico has to demonstrate it can make a greater contribution to the world economy, precisely because of the productive chains it has with the United States and Canada.” (El Economista)

🇲🇽🎓 <u>“NO YOUNG PERSON WITHOUT A UNIVERSITY”: SHEINBAUM OPENS ROSARIO CASTELLANOS TO UNAM ASPIRANTS</u>

After AI-driven fraud forced UNAM to repeat its admission exam — in person — for some 58,000 aspirants, President Sheinbaum issued the guarantee: whoever is left without a place has one, free, at the Universidad Rosario Castellanos.

158,413 young people applied to UNAM this year; 21,962 had been admitted before the irregularities were caught. The neoliberal answer to excess demand was a wall. The 4T answer: more university.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>LIBERAL DEMOCRACY IS EXHAUSTED — THE RENEWAL RUNS THROUGH MEXICO’S COMMUNITIES</u>

A new UAM book, “Las democracias: debates de actualidad,” lands as the liberal representative model collapses worldwide — a system that governs for corporations, produces Mileis and Bukeles, and hands Washington a “democracy” pretext for aggression.

Writing in Contralínea, Pablo Moctezuma draws the Mexican conclusion: stop financing the party franchises, let organized communities in workplaces, schools and neighborhoods select the candidates themselves, and bind representatives to their program — revocable if they betray it. Article 39 already says it: sovereignty resides essentially and originally in the people.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>“THE BEGINNING OF A NEW AND DANGEROUS CLIMATE ERA”: UN CHIEF</u>

António Guterres did not mince words: the fires consuming Canada and Europe are not a seasonal heat wave but “the harsh reality — the beginning of a new and dangerous climate era.”

Mexican firefighters are on the ground in Canada battling those megafires — solidarity Sheinbaum highlighted this week. Mexico shows up to fight the fires. Washington will not even say the words.
